note: status words: proved / measured / computed / cited / open / refuted

E1_entropy_force.status: computed (forward/backward passes at stored read-outs on R3 states; nothing trained)
E1_entropy_force.definition: Loss L_goal - beta * mean_{e,t} H(q_joint). For each excluded cell (10-nat rule at T=30): rms per entry of its read-out row gradient (goal; entropy per unit beta), and the sign-step direction of its step-1 fixed logit v1(beta) = -sum_n M_1n sign(g_n) - sign(g_b), g = g_goal - beta g_H (restoring if > 0). beta_release_eps = 1e-8 / rms_H (the beta at which the bonus gradient alone exceeds Adam eps immediately).

C1_gibbs_vs_naive.definition:
C1 (CPU, numpy; nothing trained). Is naive Bayes 'the fixed-prior marginal read-out with a uniform prior'?
Compares, on held-out pool episodes (exact task generator via COMMON), the goal accuracy per step of
  bayes      : A(j) = LSE_k lambda_t(j,k)                 (posterior-weighted; Gibbs identity with c = posterior)
  gibbs_unif : A(j) = mean_k lambda_t(j,k)                (fixed within-row policy c_j = uniform: Gibbs/ELBO with a
                                                           fixed variational distribution over the other latent)
  naive      : A(j) = sum_i [n_i log pbar_i(j) + (t-n_i) log(1-pbar_i(j))], pbar_i(j) = mean_k sigma(x_i(j,k))
               (the other latent re-drawn from the uniform prior for every bit at every step)
plus the Gibbs gap kappa = A_bayes - A_gibbs_unif - log R  (= KL(uniform || q(.|j)) >= 0), the mutual information
between r0 and r1 under Bayes's joint posterior per step (H(p0)+H(p1)-H(p)), and H(p).

C3_marginal_gate.definition:
C3 (CPU; computed, nothing trained). Is a MARGINAL output's restoring force gated by the value's own probability?
One goal-marginal value (target p* = 0.3) is pushed to probability q0; the other 9 values share 0.7 uniformly. The episode sits in a
batch of B = 2,000 background episodes (Dirichlet(0.5) targets, logits = log target + N(0, 0.5^2) noise), so that the networks'
loss's batch-minimum shift falls elsewhere, as in real batches. Reported: the logit gradient of that value, scaled to per-episode units
(own: x B x R because own averages over B x R values; goal CE: x B), and its ratio to q0 (a constant ratio = gated by q0).

derived.status: derived from E1 numbers (heuristic balance model; see notes section 2c-d)

beta_star_prevention.definition: beta* = c_out / (u_freeze - H_1), u_freeze ~ 11 nats step-1 surprisal (step-1 gap 7.7)

release_time_lemma_e.definition: tau = [(Phi0-X) + exp(Phi0-X) - 1]/v, X = ln(c0/eps), c0 = g e^{Phi0}, Phi0 = 14.5, v = 104 nats per Adam-time unit, lr 1e-3

fp16_release_threshold.definition: per-(e,t) bonus gradient beta q (u-H)/(B T) x loss scale > 2^-25, with max q(u-H) = 4.5e-7 (E1), B T = 240,000

toy2_first_pass.status: measured on the toy (not the network); runs stopped at 1-2k updates

C2_release.status: measured (CPU fp32 read-out training on R3 states)
C2_release.doc:
C2 (CPU, fp32): can an entropy bonus RELEASE R3's frozen read-out rows when the numerics are fp32?
Start: R3's stored read-out (joint_esn/D_critic/acc/readout_jesn.npz) on R3's frozen states (u_jesn_1, the r3 pool).
Training: fresh torch Adam (lr 1e-3, eps 1e-8; PyTorch semantics), loss = own (COMMON, = SANITY_loss) - beta * mean_{e,t}
H(softmax Y_{e,t}), batch B episodes drawn with replacement from NPRE preloaded training episodes (0..53,999), fp32.
Tracked: R3's originally excluded cells (10-nat rule at T=30 on the training-mean table F_t = W M_t + t b) and the current
ones: step-1 gaps (row criterion; min(row, column) criterion), frozen rows (median over the row of sqrt(v_hat) < eps),
held-out accuracy (2,000 episodes from 54,000..59,999) at t = 1, 10, 30, held-out mean joint entropy at t = 1 and 30.
Prediction (predictions_v2.json D1-D4, written before this ran): beta = 0.1 releases the median cell in ~0.7k updates.

C4_capture_300.doc:
C4 (CPU, fp32): the mechanism by which the start state decides the trap, at the formation stage, on three pools that differ only
in the start state (R3's read-in + frozen LSTM; joint_harness pools): r3 (R3's trained start), zero, episode_random (fresh N(0,1)
per episode).
For each pool: a joint read-out from zero, Adam (lr 1e-3, eps 1e-8), networks' loss (own), batch B from NPRE preloaded training
episodes. At updates in --at, on an analysis batch of NAN training episodes (exact full-batch gradient):
  excluded cells (10-nat rule at T=30, F_t = W M_t + t c with M_t over the preloaded episodes);
  step-1 gap (min of row and column criterion) of excluded cells;
  capture: row r's gradient g_r = m_r + e_r with m_r = sum_t Gbar_t(r) M_t (input-independent part, Gbar_t(r) = sum_e G_et(r)) and
           e_r = sum_{e,t} G_et(r)(S_et - M_t); captured entries |m_rn| > |e_rn|; f_C = |M_1|-weighted captured share;
  sign-step direction: dPhi_1 = dF_1(f) - dF_1(r) under W -= lr sign(g), c -= lr sign(g_c) for the cell r and its reference f
           (the favourite giving the smaller step-1 gap); deepening if dPhi_1 > 0;
  per-entry rms gradient of excluded rows (vs Adam eps 1e-8) and Adam's frozen rows.
Prediction (notes section 3, predictions_v2 A2/A7): with episode_random (and zero) the capture of excluded rows and the share of
deepening sign steps are lower than with r3, and step-1 gaps stay small.

C5_memorization.status: measured (CPU forward passes of run_joint read-outs)
C5_memorization.doc:
C5 (CPU; forward passes only; nothing trained). Is run_joint's B2 (per-episode random start, FIXED per episode in the pool)
limited by memorisation of the per-episode start noise?
For read-outs saved by run_joint (B2_epr_own_adam checkpoints and final; A1_r3_own_adam final for comparison on its own pool):
goal accuracy at T=30 (and t=1, 10) and the networks' loss (own) on N training episodes (0..53,999, which the read-out was
trained on) and on N held-out episodes (54,000..59,999), same pool.
Also, for B2's final read-out: the accuracy when the first K steps' states of the training episodes are replaced by those of OTHER
training episodes' starts is not possible without re-running the LSTM, so instead we report the logit-variance share carried by the
step-1..3 part of the summed state (W @ S_3 vs W @ (S_30 - S_3)) on held-out episodes: a read-out keyed to start noise puts large
weight on directions that vary mostly in u_1..u_3.

C6_noise_swap.status: measured (CPU forward passes of run_joint read-outs)
C6_noise_swap.doc:
C6 (CPU; forward passes only). Does the per-episode start noise hurt the fresh-start read-out (run_joint B2f) at TEST time, or did it
hurt LEARNING? Evaluate stored read-outs on the same 3,000 held-out episodes (54,000..59,999) with the states of three pools that differ
only in the start state (R3's read-in + frozen LSTM): episode_random (a random start per episode; the B2f read-out was trained on
fresh starts, so these are as good as fresh), zero, r3 (R3's trained start).
If B2f's read-out scores much higher on zero-start states than on random-start states, the noise hurts at test time (the read-out
learned usable evidence weights); if it stays low on zero-start states, the noise hurt learning (noise-blindness hypothesis, notes 8.2).
Also: the control (A1, trained on r3) and the start-0 read-out (C4, when present) on all three pools.

C7_gradient_snr.status: measured (CPU gradients at fixed run_joint read-outs)
C7_gradient_snr.doc:
C7 (CPU; gradients at fixed read-outs, nothing trained). Does the per-episode start noise dilute the read-out's learning signal?
At a fixed joint read-out (W, c) we draw K mini-batches of b training episodes and compute the networks'-loss gradient on W per batch,
once with zero-start states and once with random-start states (episode_random pool: an independent N(0,1) start per episode) for the
SAME episodes. Per entry: mean gradient over batches (signal) and its standard deviation (noise). Reported per state set:
  snr_median          = median over entries of |mean| / sd
  adam_kappa_median   = median of |mean| / sqrt(mean of g^2)  (the steady-state Adam step as a fraction of lr if m ~ mean, v ~ mean g^2)
  signal_rms, noise_rms over all entries; the same restricted to alive and to excluded rows (10-nat rule at T=30, this pool's M_t).
Read-outs: run_joint C4 (start-0) and B2f (fresh random starts) checkpoints at 2,000 updates, and the zero-init read-out (update 0,
W = 0, c = 0) as the formation-stage reference.
Prediction (notes 9, open item 3; written before running): random-start states give a clearly lower snr / kappa than zero-start states
at the same read-out, i.e. the start noise slows learning of the evidence weights.

C8_fixed_share.status: measured (CPU forward passes of run_joint read-outs)
C8_fixed_share.doc:
C8 (CPU; forward passes of stored run_joint read-outs, nothing trained). Test of the 'top-curvature reading' of the optimiser
ordering (notes 1, 9): does plain SGD get more of its goal-loss decrease through the fixed (episode-independent) table than Adam and
signSGD do?
For each checkpoint of the goal-CE optimiser runs on the r3 pool (D6 Adam, D6 signSGD, E6 SGD lr 0.03), on 3,000 held-out episodes:
  L_full  = goal CE of the read-out's logits L_{e,t} = W S_{e,t} + t c
  L_fixed = goal CE of the fixed table alone, F_t = W M_t + t c applied to every episode (M_t = training-episode mean of S_t)
  L_0     = goal CE of uniform beliefs (W = 0, c = 0)
  fixed_share = (L_0 - L_fixed) / (L_0 - L_full): the share of the loss decrease the fixed table achieves on its own
  also E_fix30 (coupling energy of F_30) and the fixed table's own coupling share (double-centred energy / total centred energy).
Prediction (written before running): fixed_share is highest for plain SGD at matched L_full.

harness_convergence.label: converged
harness_convergence.definition:
change of held-out accuracy (T=30) and of the held-out loss of the run's own type over the last 20% of updates.
        rise_last20 = least-squares slope over the metric records with update >= 0.8 * updates, times 0.2 * updates.
        Label: 'still rising (lower bound)' if the accuracy rise >= 0.01; else 'accuracy flat, loss still falling' if
        the loss fell by >= 2% (relative); else 'declining' if the accuracy fell by >= 0.01; else 'converged'.
